query: Which longitudinal or administrative linkage designs are most feasible in Palestine to move beyond cross‑sectional causal inference?

response.query: Which longitudinal or administrative linkage designs are most feasible in Palestine to move beyond cross‑sectional causal inference?
response.answer: In Palestine, cohort and panel studies are most feasible for causal inference beyond cross-sectional data. These designs track individuals over time, reducing bias and providing clearer causal insights.

results.title: Outcome-Wide Longitudinal Designs for Causal Inference: A New Template for Empirical Studies
results.content: August 2020 Outcome-Wide Longitudinal Designs for Causal Inference: A New Template for Empirical Studies. You will have access to both the presentation and article (if available). In this paper, we propose a new template for empirical studies intended to assess causal effects: the outcome-wide longitudinal design. We argue that the outcome-wide longitudinal design has numerous advantages over more traditional studies of single exposure-outcome relationships including results that are less subject to investigator bias, greater potential to report null effects, greater capacity to compare effect sizes, a tremendous gain in the efficiency for the research community, a greater policy relevance and a more rapid advancement of knowledge. We discuss both the practical and theoretical justification for the outcome-wide longitudinal design and also the pragmatic details of its implementation, providing publicly available R code. results.content: Can Cross-Sectional Studies Contribute to Causal Inference? Go to My NCBI account settings to confirm your email and then refresh this page. Would you like email updates of new search results? Can Cross-Sectional Studies Contribute to Causal Inference? Can Cross-Sectional Studies Contribute to Causal Inference? Cross-sectional studies-often defined as those in which exposure and outcome are assessed at the same point in time-are frequently viewed as minimally informative for causal inference. While cross-sectional studies may be susceptible to reverse causality, may be limited to assessment of disease prevalence rather than incidence, or may only provide estimates of current rather than past exposures, not all cross-sectional studies suffer these limitations. Regardless of when exposure and disease were ascertained relative to one another, a cross-sectional study may provide insights into the causal effects of exposure on disease incidence. Simply labeling a study as "cross-sectional" and assuming that 1 or more of these limitations exist and are materially important fails to recognize the need for a more nuanced assessment and risks discarding evidence that may be useful in assessing causal relationships. * Invited Commentary: Cross-Sectional Studies and Causal Inference-It's Complicated.Barnett TA, Koushik A, Schuster T.Barnett TA, et al.Am J Epidemiol. * [[May cross-sectional studies provide causal inferences?].]()Li YJ, Kan H, He YN, Li YX, Mu YT, Dai JH, Zheng YJ.Li YJ, et al.Zhonghua Liu Xing Bing Xue Za Zhi. 2020 Apr 10;41(4):589-593. * Invited Commentary: Cross-Sectional Studies and Causal Inference-It's Complicated.Barnett TA, Koushik A, Schuster T.Barnett TA, et al.Am J Epidemiol. * Measures and models for causal inference in cross-sectional studies: arguments for the appropriateness of the prevalence odds ratio and related logistic regression.Reichenheim ME, Coutinho ES.Reichenheim ME, et al.BMC Med Res Methodol. * A review of causal inference in forensic medicine.Meilia PDI, Freeman MD, Herkutanto, Zeegers MP.Meilia PDI, et al.Forensic Sci Med Pathol. doi: 10.1007/s12024-020-00220-9. * Health-Related Quality of Life and Psychosocial Variables in Women with Colorectal Pelvic Floor Dysfunction: A Cross-Sectional Study.Molina-Barea R, Slim M, Calandre EP.Molina-Barea R, et al.Healthcare (Basel). * Perceived artificial intelligence readiness in medical and health sciences education: a survey study of students in Saudi Arabia.Almalki M, Alkhamis MA, Khairallah FM, Choukou MA.Almalki M, et al.BMC Med Educ.

results.title: Cross Sectional Study vs Longitudinal Study
results.content: # Comparing Cross Sectional and Longitudinal Studies: 5 steps for choosing the right approach. Anagha Nair, "Comparing Cross Sectional and Longitudinal Studies: 5 steps for choosing the right approach." Enago Academy. The process of choosing the right research design can put ourselves at the crossroads of two distinct yet intertwined paths—cross-sectional and longitudinal studies. ## What are Cross Sectional Studies and Longitudinal Studies. However, understanding the advantages and disadvantages of cross-sectional and longitudinal studies can help you in making an informed choice while selecting your study design. ## Difference Between Cross Sectional and Longitudinal Studies. Cross-sectional studies and longitudinal studies are different in several ways. Understanding the differences in the benefits and the components of these study designs can help researchers in choosing the right design for addressing their research question. The choice between a cross-sectional and longitudinal study depends on the research questions and objectives. Deciding between a cross-sectional or longitudinal design depends on the research question at hand. ### What is the difference between a longitudinal study and a cross sectional study?▼. A longitudinal study collects data from the same subjects repeatedly over an extended period of time. A cross-sectional study collects data at one specific point in time and compares between groups or subgroups in a population rather than studying individuals over time. The key difference is that longitudinal studies track within-subject changes over time whereas cross-sectional studies provide a snapshot of between-group differences at a single time point. ### What is Cross-sectional Study?▼. Cross-sectional study is a type of observational research design in which data is collected from a population at a single point in time. A longitudinal study is a research design in which data is gathered for the same subjects repeatedly over an extended period of time. ### What is the use of cross sectional study?▼. Cross-sectional studies are useful for estimating the prevalence of diseases, conditions, traits, attitudes, risk factors, or other health metrics in a population at a specific point in time. 2.
